A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToSFiT, retaining the same algorithm, central regret analysis, and three optimization tasks. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original optimization experiments, initialization and learning-rate ablations, batched evaluations, and GPU timing measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original optimization results, expanded baseline and model comparisons, runtime measurements, and diversity and objective diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sampling, GP posterior updates, marginal likelihood maximization, VBOS objective, and standardized RLOO gradient procedure. Larger backbones and additional gradient-step settings evaluate existing components rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate password-reset FAQ refinement, protein thermal-instability optimization, and quantum circuit energy minimization. Weakened prompt context and batched protein evaluation already appear in v1. Larger models and additional comparators do not introduce new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set expands from four to seven by adding Evolutionary Search (Character), Evolutionary Search (LLM), and a prompt-based FIBO implementation in Figure 4. FIBO was only discussed as related work in v1; v3 also evaluates top-10 context variants in Figure 4d and the runtime comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen3-8B FAQ and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B circuit configurations, instruction-following models for the new baselines, and a longer fully batched runtime comparison. Figure 7 introduces a c = 1, 2, 4, 8 gradient-step sweep, while new diagnostics track generation entropy and the VBOS objective. Appendix B.3 also adds 2.0E-7 to the reported learning-rate search grid.

E4.justification: New analyses test generation diversity and collapse against actor-critic methods (Figures 5 and 10), changing objective trajectories (Figure 11), and computational versus sample efficiency (Figure 7). These substantially extend v1's initialization, learning-rate, batching, and per-step timing analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 25 random seeds, numbered 0 through 24, and report means with standard errors. v3 extends this reporting to more results without documenting a changed repeated-run design or a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds results for three comparators and larger model configurations. Figure 7 newly reports reward versus runtime and improved sample efficiency with additional gradient steps; Figures 10–11 add diversity and objective trajectories. Table 2 adds a fine-tuning time of 0.21 ± 0.01 seconds while retaining the 1.29 ± 0.05-second total. These are added results, not evidence of same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix E's Lemma 4 corrects predictive-variance indexing to use the sampled location x_t and the pre-observation posterior at t−1 consistently in the bound and derivation. The central theorem and other proofs remain substantively unchanged. The optimism inequality added to Section 2.3 restates the existing Corollary 2.

C1.justification: v1 claims improved sample efficiency with negligible computational overhead. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion in v3 claim simultaneous state-of-the-art sample and computational efficiency across Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, and evolutionary search. This adds a central comparative computational-efficiency claim; the algorithmic and regret-bound contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of why larger models benefit FAQ refinement more than discovery tasks and how FIBO's growing context limits memory and runtime. Appendix A.3 newly connects objective nonstationarity to the choice of SGD and asserts a distinction between policy and surrogate overfitting. These substantially expand the interpretation, although Section 7.1's limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds substantial comparator implementation information: tournament selection, population size, mutation rates, initial candidates, and explicit prompts. Larger-model learning rates and configuration-file information are also added. Conversely, v1's 512-token generation limit and selected task-specific SAC coefficients disappear; this is a documentation loss, not evidence that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Holland (1975) and expands positioning against evolutionary search. FIBO shifts from a related-work discussion emphasizing specialized pretraining to a comparison emphasizing in-context operation and resource limitations. Most other related-work relationships and cited works are retained.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: settings precede baselines, computational efficiency receives its own subsection, and prior-related analyses move later. Experimental results and implementation details now precede the RLOO and GP appendices, with implementation prose relocated from the main text and proof sketches separated from formal proofs.

P2.justification: Figure 4 expands from three to six panels with additional legends and revised axes. v3 adds a method-property table and plots for runtime, gradient-step sensitivity, diversity, and objective trajectories, while expanding the timing table. Existing initialization, learning-rate, and batching figures are relocated and renumbered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 materially strengthens the practical evidence: reward-versus-time comparisons and the gradient-step sweep directly test efficiency claims that v1 supported mainly with per-step timings. Diversity diagnostics, larger-model evaluations, and broader comparisons also make the empirical argument more assessable. These gains outweigh the loss of some generation and tuning details, although broad superiority claims remain limited by the tested configurations and the prompt-based, sometimes truncated FIBO implementation.
